a2a.contexts.get inkbox.api.a2a.contexts.get returns one a2a context (a conversation session) that another agent opened toward this identity, with its tasks in both directions. read
a2a.contexts.list inkbox.api.a2a.contexts.list lists a2a contexts visible to an identity, most recently active first, optionally filtered by `direction`. read
a2a.contexts.update inkbox.api.a2a.contexts.update renames an a2a context (`name`). either participant can rename it, whoever opened it. write

a2a.invitations.accept inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.accept accepts an a2a invitation (`invitation_token`) as the agent that owns the calling agent-scoped api key, connecting it to the invitation's peer agents. write

a2a.invitations.create inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.create creates an a2a invitation that lets an outside agent connect to `peer_agent_handles`; inkbox emails `recipient_email` if set, otherwise returns a link to hand off. requires an admin api key. destructive

a2a.invitations.decline inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.decline declines an a2a invitation by its `invitation_token`. connections already accepted are not affected. inkbox needs no api key for this route; the plugin still sends the connected one. write
a2a.invitations.get inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.get returns one a2a invitation issued by your organization, with its status, peer agents and email delivery state. read
a2a.invitations.list inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.list lists a2a invitations issued by your organization, newest first, optionally filtered by `status`. read

a2a.invitations.preview inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.preview shows an a2a invitation's inviter, peer agents and expiry from the raw `invitation_token` without accepting it. inkbox needs no api key for this route; the plugin still sends the connected one. read

a2a.invitations.revoke inkbox.api.a2a.invitations.revoke revokes a pending or awaiting-verification a2a invitation so it can no longer be accepted. accepted, declined or expired invitations cannot be revoked. destructive
a2a.listdirectory inkbox.api.a2a.listdirectory searches the organization's directory of a2a-enabled agent identities, including non-public cards, by text `q` or `verified_domain`. read

a2a.messages.list inkbox.api.a2a.messages.list lists a2a task messages for an identity, newest first, filterable by `direction`, `task_id`, `context_id`, `role`, peer handles, `since` or full-text `q`. read
a2a.previewcard inkbox.api.a2a.previewcard returns the agent card inkbox would publish for one of your identities, even while a2a is disabled, to review its description and skills. read

a2a.sentcontexts.get inkbox.api.a2a.sentcontexts.get returns one a2a context this identity opened toward another agent, with its tasks in both directions. returns 404 for contexts opened toward it. read
a2a.sentcontexts.list inkbox.api.a2a.sentcontexts.list lists a2a contexts this identity opened toward other agents. read
a2a.senttasks.get inkbox.api.a2a.senttasks.get returns one a2a task this identity sent to another agent, with its message history. read
a2a.senttasks.list inkbox.api.a2a.senttasks.list lists a2a tasks this identity sent to other agents, newest first, filterable by `state`, `context_id`, peer handles, `since` or full-text `q`. read
a2a.settings.get inkbox.api.a2a.settings.get returns an identity's a2a settings (enabled, public discoverability, filter mode, skills, card url) and lifetime inbound and outbound task counts. read
a2a.settings.listfororg inkbox.api.a2a.settings.listfororg lists every identity's effective a2a settings across the organization, optionally filtered by `enabled`. requires an admin api key. read

a2a.settings.update inkbox.api.a2a.settings.update updates an identity's a2a settings: `enabled`, `skills`, `allow_public_egress`, and (admin key only) `publicly_discoverable` and `filter_mode`. omitted fields are kept. write
a2a.tasks.get inkbox.api.a2a.tasks.get returns one a2a task this identity received as the worker, with its message history. use `a2a.senttasks.get` for tasks it sent. read

a2a.tasks.list inkbox.api.a2a.tasks.list lists a2a tasks visible to an identity, newest first; received tasks by default, or set `direction`. filterable by `state`, `context_id`, peer handles and `q`. read

a2a.tasks.reply inkbox.api.a2a.tasks.reply replies to a task this identity received, sending message `parts` to the requesting agent and moving the task by `intent`: progress, ask_caller, complete or fail. destructive
account.whoami inkbox.api.account.whoami returns the authenticated caller's identity and auth type, to check which organization, identity or key a request runs as. read
agentsignup.getstatus inkbox.api.agentsignup.getstatus returns the calling agent's claim status, its human owner's account state and email, and the restrictions that still apply to it. read

agentsignup.resendverification inkbox.api.agentsignup.resendverification emails the agent's human owner a new 6-digit verification code, invalidating the previous one. limited to once every 5 minutes. destructive
agentsignup.verify inkbox.api.agentsignup.verify submits the 6-digit `verification_code` the human received by email to claim the agent and unlock full sending. write

apikeys.create inkbox.api.apikeys.create creates an api key (`label`): set `scoped_identity_id` for an agent-scoped key, or omit it for an admin key with full organization access. the key value is returned only once. destructive
apikeys.getcurrent inkbox.api.apikeys.getcurrent returns metadata for the api key making the call (scope, label, status, last four characters, expiry). the key value itself is never returned. read
apikeys.revokecurrent inkbox.api.apikeys.revokecurrent revokes the api key making the call, permanently, so later requests with it fail. create a replacement key before revoking. destructive

billing.callingcountries.buy inkbox.api.billing.callingcountries.buy buys outbound calling access to countries (`country_code` or `country_codes`) with an accepted `quote` and a new `request_key`, charging the organization. reuse the key on retry; admin key only. destructive

billing.callingcountries.cancel inkbox.api.billing.callingcountries.cancel cancels renewal of a calling-country agreement (`agreement_id`). access lasts through the paid period; no prorated refund. destructive

billing.callingcountries.list inkbox.api.billing.callingcountries.list lists calling destinations with monthly prices, the organization's calling-country agreements, and the countries already included. read

billing.callingcountries.quote inkbox.api.billing.callingcountries.quote quotes the prorated charge for adding calling countries (`country_code` or `country_codes`) and returns a `quote` token to confirm the purchase. does not charge. read

billing.callingcountries.resume inkbox.api.billing.callingcountries.resume resumes renewal of a canceled calling-country agreement (`agreement_id`) before its coverage ends, at the existing price. destructive

billing.changeplan inkbox.api.billing.changeplan changes the organization's subscription `plan` (`free` cancels) and optionally its billing `interval`; requires an admin key. upgrades and moves to yearly are charged and prorated immediately. destructive

billing.createcheckoutsession inkbox.api.billing.createcheckoutsession creates a stripe checkout url for subscribing to a `plan`, returning to `success_url` or `cancel_url`. the user pays in the browser. write
billing.createportalsession inkbox.api.billing.createportalsession creates a stripe billing portal url where a person manages the organization's billing, returning to `return_url` afterwards. write
billing.getpricing inkbox.api.billing.getpricing returns usage rates and recurring add-on prices, with the organization's contracted price where one applies. read

billing.getsubscription inkbox.api.billing.getsubscription returns the organization's plan, status, billing interval, pending changes and entitlements, including whether custom email signatures are available. read

billing.getusage inkbox.api.billing.getusage returns organization usage for the current billing cycle (sms/mms, call seconds, imessage, storage, identities) by channel and identity, with remaining allowances and overage. read

billing.identitypacks.buy inkbox.api.billing.identitypacks.buy buys an identity pack (extra agent identity slots) with an accepted `quote` and a new `request_key`, charging the organization; may return a `payment_url`. requires an admin api key. destructive
billing.identitypacks.change inkbox.api.billing.identitypacks.change cancels or resumes renewal of an identity-pack agreement (`action`: cancel or resume), with a unique `request_key`. destructive
billing.identitypacks.list inkbox.api.billing.identitypacks.list lists the identity-pack offer, the organization's identity-pack agreements, identity capacity and whether it is eligible to buy. read
billing.identitypacks.quote inkbox.api.billing.identitypacks.quote quotes the price of an identity pack (extra identity slots) and returns a `quote` token for buying it. does not charge. read

billing.linebundles.buy inkbox.api.billing.linebundles.buy buys a line bundle (`code`: a voip or personal imessage line slot plus voice and sms credits) with an accepted `quote` and `request_key`, charging the organization. assigns no number; admin key only. destructive
billing.linebundles.change inkbox.api.billing.linebundles.change cancels or resumes a line-bundle agreement (`action`). canceling removes an unused line slot immediately with no refund. destructive
billing.linebundles.list inkbox.api.billing.linebundles.list lists line-bundle offers, the organization's bundle agreements, and remaining bundle voice seconds and messages. read
billing.linebundles.quote inkbox.api.billing.linebundles.quote quotes the prorated price and credits of a line bundle (`code`) and returns a `quote` token for buying it. does not charge. read
billing.settings.get inkbox.api.billing.settings.get returns the organization's monthly sms and voice overage spending cap and whether the 'sent via inkbox' email footer is removed. read

billing.settings.update inkbox.api.billing.settings.update sets the monthly sms/voice overage cap (`overage_cap_cents`; null clears it, 0 blocks overage) and/or `remove_branding_footer` (paid plans only). write

billing.setvoicepacks inkbox.api.billing.setvoicepacks sets how many call-minute packs of one size the organization holds (`pack`, `quantity`; 0 removes them); increases are invoiced immediately. paid plans and admin key only. destructive
billing.usagealerts.delete inkbox.api.billing.usagealerts.delete deletes a usage alert override (`rule_id`), restoring the default 90% alert for that quota when no other overrides remain. destructive
billing.usagealerts.list inkbox.api.billing.usagealerts.list lists the organization's usage email alerts (identities, storage, sms, voice, overage) with thresholds and whether each is a default. read

billing.usagealerts.save inkbox.api.billing.usagealerts.save creates or updates a usage email alert (`rule_id`; a new uuid adds one) for a `metric` at a percentage `threshold`, optionally for one `mailbox_id` (storage). write
compliance.brand.delete inkbox.api.compliance.brand.delete deletes the organization's 10dlc brand registration. requires an admin api key. destructive
compliance.brand.get inkbox.api.compliance.brand.get returns the organization's 10dlc brand registration and its current verification status. read

compliance.brand.register inkbox.api.compliance.brand.register registers the organization's 10dlc brand (business details for us sms) for verification. one brand per organization; asynchronous, so check its status afterwards. destructive
compliance.brand.resendtwofactoremail inkbox.api.compliance.brand.resendtwofactoremail resends the verification (2fa) email for the organization's 10dlc brand. destructive

compliance.brand.sendsmsotp inkbox.api.compliance.brand.sendsmsotp texts a one-time pin to the brand's phone to verify a sole-proprietor 10dlc brand; confirm it with `compliance.brand.verifysmsotp`. destructive
compliance.brand.update inkbox.api.compliance.brand.update replaces the organization's 10dlc brand details; all required business fields must be sent again. requires an admin api key. write
compliance.brand.verifysmsotp inkbox.api.compliance.brand.verifysmsotp verifies the 10dlc brand with the one-time pin (`otp_pin`) received by sms. write
compliance.campaign.delete inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.delete deletes the organization's 10dlc campaign, which also stops its monthly fee. requires an admin api key. destructive
compliance.campaign.get inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.get returns the organization's 10dlc campaign and its carrier review status (`campaignstatus`). read
compliance.campaign.getactive inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.getactive returns whether the organization has selected its own 10dlc campaign (`active: true`) or inkbox's default campaign. read

compliance.campaign.register inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.register submits the organization's 10dlc campaign (use case, sample messages, opt-in/opt-out keywords, policy links) for carrier review. costs $20/month once approved. destructive

compliance.campaign.resubmit inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.resubmit replaces the 10dlc campaign with a complete new registration and a new campaign id; local numbers return to inkbox's default campaign during review. destructive

compliance.campaign.setactive inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.setactive switches the organization's local us numbers to its own approved 10dlc campaign (`active: true`) or back to inkbox's default. runs asynchronously. destructive
compliance.campaign.update inkbox.api.compliance.campaign.update updates the 10dlc campaign's `help_message`, `message_flow` and sample messages. requires an admin api key. write

compliance.uploadoptinevidence inkbox.api.compliance.uploadoptinevidence uploads an image (`file`, max 5 mib) of your sms opt-in flow and returns a public url to cite in the campaign's `message_flow`. write
contacts.bulkdelete inkbox.api.contacts.bulkdelete deletes 1 to 1,000 contacts by `contact_ids` and returns a result for each. destructive

contacts.communicationpolicy.get inkbox.api.contacts.communicationpolicy.get returns a contact's communication policy for an agent identity (`identity_id`): per-address inbound/outbound allow or block and field visibility. read

contacts.communicationpolicy.preview inkbox.api.contacts.communicationpolicy.preview previews what one agent identity (`identity_id`) can see of a contact and whether it may email or phone it in each direction. requires an admin api key. read

contacts.communicationpolicy.set inkbox.api.contacts.communicationpolicy.set sets which of a contact's `addresses` an agent identity (`identity_id`) may use inbound and outbound, and its `visibility`, given the current `expected_revision`. requires an admin api key. write
contacts.create inkbox.api.contacts.create creates a contact with names, company, emails, phones, addresses and custom fields. at least one name field or `company_name` is required. write
contacts.createwithpermissions inkbox.api.contacts.createwithpermissions creates a contact and sets one agent's access `permissions` in a single transaction. requires an admin api key. write
contacts.delete inkbox.api.contacts.delete deletes one contact by `contact_id`. use `contacts.bulkdelete` to delete up to 1,000 at once. destructive
contacts.exportvcard inkbox.api.contacts.exportvcard downloads one contact (`contact_id`) as a vcard (.vcf) file. read
contacts.exportvcards inkbox.api.contacts.exportvcards exports 1 to 25 contacts (`contact_ids`) as a single vcard document. read
contacts.facts.create inkbox.api.contacts.facts.create adds a memory (`content`, `kind`) to a contact. requires an admin api key; agent-scoped keys cannot write memories. write
contacts.facts.delete inkbox.api.contacts.facts.delete deletes one memory from a contact. requires an admin api key. destructive
contacts.facts.get inkbox.api.contacts.facts.get returns one contact memory with its citations, including a memory whose deadline has passed. read
contacts.facts.list inkbox.api.contacts.facts.list lists a contact's memories, most recently updated first. set `include_expired` to include memories past their deadline. read

contacts.facts.resolvecitation inkbox.api.contacts.facts.resolvecitation resolves a memory's citation to its source id, locator and url, after rechecking that the caller can still access that correspondence. read
contacts.facts.update inkbox.api.contacts.facts.update edits a contact memory's `content` or moves it to another `kind`. requires an admin api key. write
contacts.get inkbox.api.contacts.get returns one contact by `contact_id`, limited to the fields the caller is permitted to see. read

contacts.getcorrespondence inkbox.api.contacts.getcorrespondence returns email, sms, imessage, whatsapp and call history between one contact and an agent identity, filterable by `channels`, `after`/`before` and per-channel limits. read
contacts.import inkbox.api.contacts.import imports up to 2,500 contacts from a vcard body (max 10 mib). pass `x-vcard-preview-hash` from a preview to fail if the data or conflicts changed. write
contacts.list inkbox.api.contacts.list lists contacts visible to the caller, with name search `q`, `order` and `review_status` filters. read
contacts.lookup inkbox.api.contacts.lookup finds contacts by one field: exact `email` or `phone`, or partial match with `email_contains`, `email_domain` or `phone_contains`. read
contacts.merge inkbox.api.contacts.merge merges duplicate contacts (`losing_contact_ids`) into this contact, combining identifiers, correspondence and memories. requires an admin api key. destructive

contacts.previewimport inkbox.api.contacts.previewimport validates a vcard batch (`vcard`) and reports conflicts with existing contacts, without creating any. returns a `preview_hash` for the import. read
contacts.update inkbox.api.contacts.update updates a contact with json merge-patch: sent fields replace, null clears, omitted fields are kept. write

domains.create inkbox.api.domains.create registers a custom email sending domain (`domain`) and returns the dns records to publish. an apex with existing mx records needs `apex_mx_acknowledged` to displace that mail provider. write

domains.delete inkbox.api.domains.delete deletes a custom sending domain: sending and receiving stop at once, and it can be restored for 24 hours before deletion is permanent. fails while mailboxes still use it. destructive
domains.forcedelete inkbox.api.domains.forcedelete deletes a custom sending domain (`domain_id`) by force, bypassing the normal delete flow and its restore window; treat it as permanent. destructive
domains.get inkbox.api.domains.get returns one custom sending domain with its status and required dns records. read
domains.getdnsrecords inkbox.api.domains.getdnsrecords returns the dns records (ownership txt, mail routing, dkim and others) to publish at the registrar for a custom sending domain. read
domains.gethealth inkbox.api.domains.gethealth returns a custom sending domain's health: its status and the current check result for each required dns record. read
domains.list inkbox.api.domains.list lists the organization's custom email sending domains, optionally filtered by lifecycle `status`. read
domains.restore inkbox.api.domains.restore restores a custom sending domain that is still in its 24-hour deletion grace period. write

domains.rotatedkim inkbox.api.domains.rotatedkim starts a dkim key rotation for a custom sending domain and returns the new selector and txt value to publish; the old key stays active until the new one verifies. destructive

domains.setdefault inkbox.api.domains.setdefault makes a verified custom domain (`domain_name`) the organization's default for new mailboxes; pass `inkboxmail.com` to revert. requires an admin api key. write
domains.verify inkbox.api.domains.verify re-checks a custom sending domain's dns records now and returns its updated status. write

hostedchat.answerinteraction inkbox.api.hostedchat.answerinteraction answers a pending tool approval or question in a hosted-agent conversation with `response` (for example approve_once or deny) at `expected_version`; only the first valid answer counts. write
hostedchat.conversations.create inkbox.api.hostedchat.conversations.create starts a new chat conversation with an identity's hosted agent, with an optional `title`. write

hostedchat.conversations.get inkbox.api.hostedchat.conversations.get returns a snapshot of a hosted-agent conversation: recent items, pending approvals, the current turn, and cursors for paging and events. read

hostedchat.conversations.list inkbox.api.hostedchat.conversations.list lists chat conversations with an identity's hosted agent, optionally filtered by `origin` (`chat`, `communication` or `schedule`). read

hostedchat.conversations.listmessages inkbox.api.hostedchat.conversations.listmessages lists older items of a hosted-agent conversation, paging with `after` and a `snapshot` token from the conversation snapshot. read

hostedchat.turns.cancel inkbox.api.hostedchat.turns.cancel requests cancellation of a running turn in a hosted-agent conversation. write

hostedchat.turns.get inkbox.api.hostedchat.turns.get returns the status of one turn in a hosted-agent conversation (queued, running, waiting_for_input, completed, failed and so on) and any blocker. read
hostedworkspace.environment.get inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.environment.get lists environment variables set on the hosted agent's computer; secret values are masked. read

hostedworkspace.environment.update inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.environment.update sets (`set`) or removes (`remove`) environment variables on the hosted agent's computer at `expected_version`. changes apply to new processes. write
hostedworkspace.get inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.get returns the hosted agent's computer state, agent readiness, capabilities, funding and allowed actions. read
hostedworkspace.getoperation inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.getoperation returns the progress and result of a workspace operation (start, stop, pause, resume, resize, terminal) by `operation_id`. read
hostedworkspace.getusage inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.getusage returns current cpu, memory and disk usage of the hosted agent's computer. read
hostedworkspace.getusagehistory inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.getusagehistory returns cpu, memory and disk usage history of the hosted agent's computer over a `window` (1h, 24h, 7d or 30d). read
hostedworkspace.ports.get inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.ports.get returns the hosted agent's public url, default port and exposed ports. read

hostedworkspace.schedules.delete inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.schedules.delete deletes a hosted-agent schedule, given its current `expected_revision`. destructive
hostedworkspace.schedules.list inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.schedules.list lists the hosted agent's schedules with their registration status. read
hostedworkspace.schedules.listoccurrences inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.schedules.listoccurrences lists past runs of one hosted-agent schedule and the conversation that holds their output. read
hostedworkspace.schedules.preview inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.schedules.preview previews the next run times for a schedule `timing` (cron, interval or once) without saving anything. read

hostedworkspace.schedules.update inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.schedules.update edits, pauses (`enabled: false`) or resumes a hosted-agent schedule via `fields`, given its current `expected_revision`. write
hostedworkspace.terminals.close inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.terminals.close closes a terminal session on the hosted agent's computer. write

hostedworkspace.terminals.createticket inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.terminals.createticket returns a short-lived ticket and url to attach to a terminal session on the hosted agent's computer. write
hostedworkspace.terminals.list inkbox.api.hostedworkspace.terminals.list lists terminal sessions on the hosted agent's computer. read

hosting.calltool inkbox.api.hosting.calltool sends a json-rpc mcp request (`method`, `params`) to the identity's hosted tools endpoint, for example to list or call the tools its hosted agent uses. destructive

identities.avatar.upload inkbox.api.identities.avatar.upload uploads or replaces an identity's avatar image (`file`, multipart), used as the photo on the contact cards it shares. write

identities.connectimessagenumber inkbox.api.identities.connectimessagenumber attaches an existing dedicated imessage number (`imessage_number_id`) to an identity. write

identities.contactaccess.update inkbox.api.identities.contactaccess.update sets an identity's access to one contact by group: `email` and `phone` visibility and inbound/outbound contactable lists (replacing that side), `profile` and `memories`. admin api key only. write

identities.getcurrent inkbox.api.identities.getcurrent returns the identity the calling agent-scoped api key belongs to. read
identities.list inkbox.api.identities.list lists all identities in the organization, newest first, each with its mailbox, tunnel, phone number and imessage line. read

identities.mailcontactrules.get inkbox.api.identities.mailcontactrules.get returns one email allow or block rule of an identity by `rule_id`. read

identities.mailcontactrules.update inkbox.api.identities.mailcontactrules.update changes an email contact rule's `action` or `direction`, or edits one side with `apply_to`. requires an admin api key. write

identities.phonecontactrules.create inkbox.api.identities.phonecontactrules.create creates a phone allow or block rule for an e.164 number (`match_target`) covering an identity's sms, calls, imessage and whatsapp, optionally per `direction`. admin api key only. write
identities.phonecontactrules.delete inkbox.api.identities.phonecontactrules.delete deletes a phone contact rule from an identity. requires an admin api key. destructive
identities.phonecontactrules.get inkbox.api.identities.phonecontactrules.get returns one phone allow or block rule of an identity by `rule_id`. read

identities.phonecontactrules.list inkbox.api.identities.phonecontactrules.list lists an identity's phone allow and block rules, newest first, filterable by `action`, `match_type` and `direction`. read

identities.phonecontactrules.update inkbox.api.identities.phonecontactrules.update changes a phone contact rule's `action` or `direction`, or edits one side with `apply_to`; the number cannot change. requires an admin api key. write

identities.slackcontactrules.delete inkbox.api.identities.slackcontactrules.delete deletes a slack contact rule from an identity. requires an admin api key. destructive
identities.slackcontactrules.get inkbox.api.identities.slackcontactrules.get returns one slack allow or block rule of an identity by `rule_id`. read

identities.slackcontactrules.list inkbox.api.identities.slackcontactrules.list lists an identity's slack allow and block rules, filterable by `action`, `match_type` (exact_user or workspace) and `direction`. read

identities.slackcontactrules.update inkbox.api.identities.slackcontactrules.update changes a slack contact rule's `action` or `direction`, or edits one side with `apply_to`. requires an admin api key. write

imessage.contactrules.list inkbox.api.imessage.contactrules.list lists an identity's imessage/phone-list allow and block rules, newest first, filterable by `action`, `match_type` and `direction`. read

imessage.contactrules.listfororg inkbox.api.imessage.contactrules.listfororg lists imessage/phone-list contact rules across every identity the key can see, optionally narrowed to one `agent_identity_id`. requires an admin api key. read

imessage.contactrules.update inkbox.api.imessage.contactrules.update changes an imessage/phone-list contact rule's `action` or `direction`, or edits one side with `apply_to`; the number cannot change. requires an admin api key. write

inbound.sources.create inkbox.api.inbound.sources.create creates an inbound webhook source (`name`) for a hosted agent and returns the url third parties post events to, with optional `signature` checking and `handler` (agent or script). write
inbound.sources.delete inkbox.api.inbound.sources.delete deletes an inbound source and all its events; its url stops working. destructive

mail.imports.cancel inkbox.api.mail.imports.cancel cancels a pending, queued or running mail import job; messages already imported stay in the mailbox. write

mail.imports.get inkbox.api.mail.imports.get returns a mail import job's status and counters (processed, imported, duplicates, failed). read
mail.imports.list inkbox.api.mail.imports.list lists a mailbox's email import jobs, newest first. read
mail.imports.reissueuploadurl inkbox.api.mail.imports.reissueuploadurl issues a fresh upload target for a mail import job whose previous upload url expired before the file was uploaded. write
mail.imports.start inkbox.api.mail.imports.start validates the uploaded file and queues a mail import job to run. write

notes.access.grant inkbox.api.notes.access.grant grants an agent identity (`identity_id`) read and edit access to a note. write

phone.media.getplayback inkbox.api.phone.media.getplayback returns an audio attachment from a text message (`media_id`) converted for browser playback. read

authorization quaderno.api.authorization which account this key belongs to: `identity.href` is that account’s base url, so this is how a caller finds the subdomain to pass as `account`. also returns the default api version. read

contacts.create quaderno.api.contacts.create adds a customer. `first_name` is required, and holds the company name for a `company`. give an `email` if documents will be delivered to this contact. write

contacts.delete quaderno.api.contacts.delete removes a customer. quaderno refuses with 422 while the contact still has documents attached, so invoices must be voided first. answers 204 with no body. destructive

contacts.get quaderno.api.contacts.get one customer by id. an unknown id answers **401**, not 404, with “unauthorized access or contact does not exist”; the plugin reports it as `not_found_or_denied`. read
contacts.list quaderno.api.contacts.list customers, newest first, answered as a bare array. search with `q` and page with `created_before`; `next_created_before` carries the next cursor. read
contacts.update quaderno.api.contacts.update changes a customer. fields left out are left unchanged by the api, not cleared. write

credits.create quaderno.api.credits.create issues a credit note against an existing invoice, by `invoice_id`, and records the refund. it credits the whole invoice unless `credited_amount` is given. it consumes a document number and cannot be deleted, only voided. write

credits.deliver quaderno.api.credits.deliver emails the credit note to the address on file for its contact. a get that mutates, so it is a write and is never replayed. answers `delivered: true`. write
credits.get quaderno.api.credits.get one credit note by id, with its lines, payments and the document it credits. read
credits.list quaderno.api.credits.list credit notes, newest first, as a bare array. a voided invoice leaves one of these beside it. read

credits.update quaderno.api.credits.update changes the administrative fields of a credit note: `notes`, `payment_details` and `tag_list`. amounts, lines and the customer are immutable once it is issued. write
credits.void quaderno.api.credits.void voids a credit note. `void_reason` is required, exactly as for an invoice. destructive

invoices.create quaderno.api.invoices.create issues an invoice and **allocates a document number**, which is not recoverable: invoices cannot be deleted, only voided. passing `payment_method` records a full payment immediately and marks it paid. needs a `contact` id and at least one line item. write

invoices.deliver quaderno.api.invoices.deliver sends the invoice by email to the address on file for its contact, using the account template. a **get that mutates**, so it is a write here and never replayed: delivering twice emails twice. the contact needs a valid email. answers no document, only `delivered: true`. write
invoices.get quaderno.api.invoices.get one invoice with its lines, taxes and payments. an unknown id answers 401 rather than 404. read
invoices.list quaderno.api.invoices.list invoices, newest first, as a bare array. filter by date, state, contact or processor id, search with `q`, and page with `created_before`. read
invoices.markuncollectible quaderno.api.invoices.markuncollectible marks an unpaid invoice as bad debt. reversible by recording a payment later, unlike a void. write
invoices.recordpayment quaderno.api.invoices.recordpayment records a payment against an invoice; reaching the total marks it paid. this creates a real financial record, not a note. write

invoices.update quaderno.api.invoices.update changes an invoice. only the fields you send are changed. an issued invoice is legally immutable: quaderno then accepts only `notes`, `payment_details` and `tag_list`, so correct anything else by voiding it and issuing a new one. write

invoices.void quaderno.api.invoices.void reverses an invoice the way tax law requires. it cannot be deleted: voiding records an `offset` payment for the full amount and issues a credit note beside it. `void_reason` is required and the api answers 422 without it. destructive
jurisdictions.get quaderno.api.jurisdictions.get one tax jurisdiction by id, naming the country and any region whose tax rules apply. read

jurisdictions.list quaderno.api.jurisdictions.list every tax jurisdiction quaderno knows, about 290 rows, as a bare array. verified live: this route ignores `limit` and always returns the full list. read
ping quaderno.api.ping checks that the key and account name are valid. the docs say it does not consume an api call. answers `{"status":"ok"}`. read
products.create quaderno.api.products.create adds a product. `name`, `code` and `unit_cost` are required, and `kind` is `one_off` or `subscription`, not the value the spec’s example suggests. write
products.delete quaderno.api.products.delete removes a product. existing documents keep the line they were issued with, so past invoices are unaffected. destructive
products.get quaderno.api.products.get one product by id, with its price, tax class and the currency it is sold in. read
products.list quaderno.api.products.list your product catalogue, newest first, from the `/items` route. a bare array; page with `created_before`. read
products.update quaderno.api.products.update changes a product. existing documents keep the line they were issued with, so past invoices are unaffected. write
proformas.accept quaderno.api.proformas.accept marks a proforma accepted. a state change the customer would normally trigger; reversible with `proformas.revert`. write

proformas.convert quaderno.api.proformas.convert converts an accepted proforma into a real invoice, which **consumes an invoice number and cannot be undone**. only a proforma in the accepted state can be converted. returns the new invoice under `invoice`. write
proformas.create quaderno.api.proformas.create creates a proforma. unlike an invoice this is not a tax document, so it does not consume an invoice number. write
proformas.decline quaderno.api.proformas.decline marks a proforma declined. reversible with `proformas.revert`. write

proformas.deliver quaderno.api.proformas.deliver emails the proforma to the address on file for its contact. a get that mutates, so it is a write and is never replayed. answers `delivered: true`. write
proformas.get quaderno.api.proformas.get one proforma by id, with its lines and the state it was accepted or declined in. read
proformas.list quaderno.api.proformas.list proforma invoices, newest first, as a bare array. a proforma is not a tax document, so it carries no invoice number. read
proformas.revert quaderno.api.proformas.revert puts an accepted or declined proforma back to its open state. write

proformas.update quaderno.api.proformas.update changes a proforma. only the id is required. an accepted or invoiced proforma cannot be changed. it stays a proforma until `proformas.convert` issues a real invoice. write

receipts.create quaderno.api.receipts.create issues a receipt for a sale that is already paid, so `payment_method` is required. like an invoice, it consumes a document number and cannot be deleted or updated, only voided. write
receipts.deliver quaderno.api.receipts.deliver emails the receipt to the address on file for its contact. a get that mutates, so it is a write and is never replayed. answers `delivered: true`. write
receipts.get quaderno.api.receipts.get one receipt by id, with its lines, payments and the invoice it settles. read
receipts.list quaderno.api.receipts.list receipts, newest first, as a bare array. filter by a `date` range or `contact`, and page with `created_before`. read
receipts.void quaderno.api.receipts.void voids a receipt. `void_reason` is required, as for an invoice. destructive
taxcodes.get quaderno.api.taxcodes.get one tax code by its identifier, such as `standard`. read
taxcodes.list quaderno.api.taxcodes.list the tax codes available on the account, as a bare array. this route honours `limit`, unlike `jurisdictions.list`. read

taxids.validate quaderno.api.taxids.validate checks a vat or tax number against the country’s registry. `valid` is true or false, or null when the registry could not be reached, which does not mean the number is invalid. read

taxrates.calculate quaderno.api.taxrates.calculate the tax rate quaderno would charge for a customer country and tax code, with the resulting total. `tax_code` and `amount` are required from api version 20210316, which this plugin targets. read

transactions.create quaderno.api.transactions.create records a sale or a refund in one call: it creates the document and its payment together, which is what distinguishes it from `invoices.create`. the body is not an invoice body: the buyer is `customer`, each line carries its total as `amount`, and `payment.method` is required. a real financial record. write

webhooks.list quaderno.api.webhooks.list the webhook subscriptions on the account, with the events each one receives. read only here: this plugin registers no inbound handler. the signing secret (`auth_key`) is left out of the result. read

agentactions.generate sanity.api.agentactions.generate have sanity's ai write content into a document's fields from an instruction, following the schema. writes to the draft unless forcepublishedwrite; nowrite returns it without saving. costs one sanity ai credit. write
agentactions.prompt sanity.api.agentactions.prompt ask sanity's ai a question, optionally about documents passed as params, and get text or json back. writes nothing. costs one sanity ai credit. read

agentactions.transform sanity.api.agentactions.transform have sanity's ai rewrite a document's existing content by an instruction (tone, length, style), in place or into another document. costs one sanity ai credit. write
agentactions.translate sanity.api.agentactions.translate have sanity's ai translate a document into another language, usually into a new document. costs one sanity ai credit. write
assets.upload sanity.api.assets.upload upload an image or file (base64, up to 25 mb) as a sanity asset and get its asset document and cdn url, ready to reference from a document. write
datasets.create sanity.api.datasets.create create an empty dataset in the project. needs an administrator token. write
datasets.delete sanity.api.datasets.delete delete a dataset with every document and asset in it, for good. needs the name twice and an administrator token. destructive
datasets.list sanity.api.datasets.list the project's datasets and whether each is public. read
documents.create sanity.api.documents.create create a document as a draft (default) or, with publish: true, publish it at once. returns its id and draft id. write

documents.delete sanity.api.documents.delete delete up to 100 documents, published and draft together. documents that reference them must drop the references first. with purge, they also leave the history. destructive

documents.discarddraft sanity.api.documents.discarddraft throw away a document's unpublished changes (its draft). the published version stays. with purge, the draft also leaves the history. destructive

documents.edit sanity.api.documents.edit change a document the way the studio does: the patch goes to its draft, made from the published version if needed, and nothing goes live until documents.publish (or publish: true). write
documents.get sanity.api.documents.get fetch up to 100 documents by exact id (drafts.<id> for a draft). ids that are missing or unreadable come back in omitted. read
documents.history sanity.api.documents.history a document as it stood at a revision or a point in time. how far back depends on the plan's history retention. read

documents.mutate sanity.api.documents.mutate apply raw sanity mutations (create, createorreplace, createifnotexists, patch, delete, by id or by query) in one transaction. for anything documents.create, edit, patch and delete can't express. destructive

documents.patch sanity.api.documents.patch patch one exact document id directly and get it back. a published id changes the live document at once; use documents.edit to go through a draft. ifrevisionid guards against overwriting someone else's change. write
documents.publish sanity.api.documents.publish publish a document's draft: the draft replaces the published version and goes away. fails when there is no draft. write
documents.query sanity.api.documents.query run a groq query against a dataset and get its result. reads published documents unless perspective says otherwise. pass user input as params. read
documents.transactions sanity.api.documents.transactions the transactions that changed some documents: when, by whom and which revisions, optionally with each mutation. read
documents.unpublish sanity.api.documents.unpublish take a published document off the published perspective; its content stays as a draft. write

schemas.list sanity.api.schemas.list the schemas deployed to a dataset: their ids (the schemaid agent actions take) and each type's fields. pass type for one type's full definition. read this before writing documents of a type you don't know. read
webhooks.attempts sanity.api.webhooks.attempts recent delivery attempts of a webhook with the status your endpoint answered, to debug failing deliveries. read

webhooks.create sanity.api.webhooks.create create a webhook that posts to a url when documents matching a groq filter are created, updated or deleted. set a secret so deliveries can be verified. write
webhooks.delete sanity.api.webhooks.delete delete a webhook; deliveries stop at once. destructive
webhooks.list sanity.api.webhooks.list the project's groq-powered webhooks: url, dataset, filter, projection and whether each is signed (never the secret). read
webhooks.update sanity.api.webhooks.update change a webhook's url, filter, projection, events or secret, or pause and resume it with disabled. write

documents.changed sanity.webhooks.documents.changed a groq-powered webhook fired: a document matching its filter was created, updated or deleted. the body is the webhook's projection; the operation, document id and dataset come from its headers. only signed deliveries are accepted.

disputes.createevidencefile square.api.disputes.createevidencefile uploads a file to use as evidence in a dispute challenge. the endpoint accepts http multipart/form-data file uploads in heic, heif, jpeg, pdf, png, and tiff formats. requires idempotency_key; pass the same key to retry safely. write

disputes.getevidence square.api.disputes.getevidence returns the metadata for the evidence specified in the request url path. read
disputes.list square.api.disputes.list returns a list of disputes associated with a particular account. read

disputes.submitevidence square.api.disputes.submitevidence submits evidence to the cardholder's bank. cannot be undone. destructive

invoices.cancel square.api.invoices.cancel cancels an invoice. the seller cannot collect payments for the canceled invoice. pass the invoice's current version; every committed change, including adding or removing an attachment, increments it. read it with invoices.get. cannot be undone. destructive

invoices.create square.api.invoices.create creates a draft invoice for an order created using the orders api. give delivery_method (recommended) or the deprecated request_method on each payment request; the schema does not require delivery_method for that reason. pass the same idempotency_key to retry safely. write

invoices.createattachment square.api.invoices.createattachment uploads a file and attaches it to an invoice. this endpoint accepts http multipart/form-data file uploads with a json `request` part and a `file` part. notifies the customer by email or text message when the invoice's delivery_method is email or sms; the api has no option to skip this. pass the same idempotency_key to retry safely. destructive

invoices.delete square.api.invoices.delete deletes the specified invoice. when an invoice is deleted, the associated order status changes to canceled. if you pass version, it must be the current one; every committed change, including adding or removing an attachment, increments it. read it with invoices.get. cannot be undone. destructive

invoices.deleteattachment square.api.invoices.deleteattachment removes an attachment from an invoice and permanently deletes the file. attachments can be removed only from invoices in the `draft`, `scheduled`, `unpaid`, or `partially_paid` state. notifies the customer by email or text message when the invoice's delivery_method is email or sms; the api has no option to skip this. cannot be undone. destructive
invoices.get square.api.invoices.get retrieves an invoice by invoice id. read

invoices.list square.api.invoices.list returns a list of invoices for a given location. the response is paginated. if truncated, the response includes a `cursor` that you use in a subsequent request to retrieve the next set of invoices. read

invoices.publish square.api.invoices.publish publishes the specified draft invoice. sends the invoice to the customer and may charge the card on file; cancel with invoices.cancel. pass the invoice's current version; every committed change, including adding or removing an attachment, increments it. read it with invoices.get. moves money. pass the same idempotency_key to retry safely. destructive
invoices.search square.api.invoices.search searches for invoices from a location specified in the filter. you can optionally specify customers in the filter for whom to retrieve invoices. read

invoices.update square.api.invoices.update updates an invoice. this endpoint supports sparse updates, so you only need to specify the fields you want to change along with the required `version` field. some restrictions apply to updating invoices. notifies the customer by email or text message when the invoice's delivery_method is email or sms; the api has no option to skip this. pass the invoice's current version; every committed change, including adding or removing an attachment, increments it. read it with invoices.get. pass the same idempotency_key to retry safely. destructive

deviceinvites.accept tailscale.api.deviceinvites.accept accept a device share invite from another tailnet into this key's tailnet, by its invite url or code. the shared device then appears in devices.list. needs a user's api access token: a share belongs to a user, so an oauth client can't accept one. write

deviceinvites.create tailscale.api.deviceinvites.create share a device with people outside the tailnet. each invite gives an invite url to send; with email set, tailscale emails the invite itself. allowexitnode lets the recipient use the device as an exit node; multiuse lets several people accept one link. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. destructive
deviceinvites.delete tailscale.api.deviceinvites.delete delete a device share invite; its link stops working. write
deviceinvites.get tailscale.api.deviceinvites.get get a device share invite: its invite url, who accepted it and when. read

deviceinvites.list tailscale.api.deviceinvites.list list the share invites for a device (who it was shared with, accepted or not); null when there are none. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. read
deviceinvites.resend tailscale.api.deviceinvites.resend email a device share invite again to the address it was created for. destructive

devices.authorize tailscale.api.devices.authorize approve (authorized: true) or revoke approval for (authorized: false) a device when the tailnet requires device approval. revoking cuts the device's access until it is approved again. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.delete tailscale.api.devices.delete remove a device from the tailnet. it loses access at once and must be signed in again (with a new auth key or login) to rejoin. cannot be undone. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. destructive

devices.expirekey tailscale.api.devices.expirekey expire a device's node key now: the device is disconnected until someone signs in on it again. use it to cut off a lost or compromised machine. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. destructive

devices.list tailscale.api.devices.list list the devices in the tailnet: name, hostname, tailscale ips, owner, os, client version, tags, last seen, key expiry, authorized. pass fields: "all" to add advertised and enabled routes, posture and connectivity details. filters narrows the list on the server by exact match on top-level device fields, all of them required to match (for example { tags: ["tag:prod"], isephemeral: true }). read

devices.postureattributes.batchupdate tailscale.api.devices.postureattributes.batchupdate set or delete custom posture attributes on many devices in one call. a null value deletes that attribute. applied all together or not at all. write

devices.postureattributes.delete tailscale.api.devices.postureattributes.delete delete a custom posture attribute (custom:...) from a device. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.postureattributes.get tailscale.api.devices.postureattributes.get get a device's posture attributes: tailscale's own (node:os, node:tsversion, node:tsreleasetrack, ...) and custom ones (custom:<name>) set through the api or a posture integration. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. read

devices.postureattributes.set tailscale.api.devices.postureattributes.set set a custom posture attribute on a device. attributekey must start with custom: (for example custom:agentapproved); value is a string, number or boolean. expiry (rfc 3339) makes it lapse on its own. policy postures can then allow or deny access on it. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.routes.list tailscale.api.devices.routes.list list the subnet routes and exit-node routes a device advertises and which of them are enabled. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. read

devices.routes.set tailscale.api.devices.routes.set set which of the routes a device advertises are enabled (subnet routes, and 0.0.0.0/0 plus ::/0 for an exit node). replaces the enabled list: routes left out are turned off. only routes the device advertises can be enabled. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.setip tailscale.api.devices.setip change a device's tailscale ipv4 address to an unused one in the tailnet's range (100.64.0.0/10 by default). existing connections to the old address break and must reconnect to the new one. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.setname tailscale.api.devices.setname rename a device: its magicdns name becomes <name>.<tailnet>.ts.net. pass name: "" to go back to the machine's own hostname. connections using the old name stop resolving. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.settags tailscale.api.devices.settags replace a device's acl tags (tag:server, tag:mcp, ...). each tag must be defined in the policy file and owned by the caller (tagowners). tagging a user's device turns it into a tagged device that no longer belongs to that user, and the access rules for its tags apply from then on. pass tags: [] to remove every tag. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

devices.updatekey tailscale.api.devices.updatekey turn key expiry off (keyexpirydisabled: true) or back on for a device, for servers that should stay signed in. deviceid is the device `id` or `nodeid` from devices.list. write

dns.configuration.set tailscale.api.dns.configuration.set replace the tailnet's whole dns configuration in one call (nameservers, split dns, search paths, preferences). write

dns.searchpaths.list tailscale.api.dns.searchpaths.list list the dns search domains pushed to devices. read

keys.delete tailscale.api.keys.delete revoke a key. devices already added with an auth key stay; anything using a revoked api token or oauth client stops working. cannot be undone. destructive

policyfile.get tailscale.api.policyfile.get get the tailnet's policy file (acls or grants, groups, tagowners, autoapprovers, postures, tests). format "hujson" (the default) keeps comments and returns the text; "json" returns an object without comments. etag is the version: pass it as ifmatch to policyfile.set so another edit made in between is not overwritten. details: true also returns warnings and errors. read

policyfile.preview tailscale.api.policyfile.preview show which rules of the policy file you pass apply to a user (type "user", previewfor their email) or a destination (type "ipport", previewfor "100.101.102.103:443"), without saving anything. policy is required: pass a draft, or the text from policyfile.get to preview the current file. read

policyfile.set tailscale.api.policyfile.set replace the tailnet's policy file, as hujson text (keeps comments) or a json object. it controls who can reach what across the whole tailnet, so run policyfile.validate first, and pass ifmatch with the etag from policyfile.get: tailscale then refuses the write if the file changed since. tests in the file must pass or nothing is saved. destructive

policyfile.validate tailscale.api.policyfile.validate check a draft policy file without saving it: pass policy (hujson text or object) to parse it and run its tests, or tests (at least one) to run acl tests against the current file. null or an empty message means everything passed. problems still answer 200: message holds the parse error, or "test(s) failed" with each failing test in data. read
